Welcome! I’m glad you’re here, because together, we’re about to set off on a journey that’s as much about life as it is about running.
Have you ever wondered what long-distance running can reveal about creativity, persistence, or even the way we approach each day? As we explore the pages of "What I Talk About When I Talk About Running," woven so thoughtfully by Haruki Murakami, we’ll discover how the steady rhythm of running becomes a window into the deeper currents of endurance, imagination, and self-discovery.
It’s not just about how fast or how far we go. It’s about that quiet determination to keep moving—especially when the road gets tough. Every solitary step, every mile, brings new reflections on aging, meaning, and the pursuit of something deeply personal.
Along the way, you’ll notice how the worlds of art and athletics merge—how the discipline of lacing up your shoes mirrors the discipline of sitting down to write. Murakami invites us to see that both running and writing are journeys made up of countless small choices, steady effort, and a willingness to embrace solitude and resilience.
So, as we head out together, let’s open ourselves to the lessons waiting with every stride. We’ll uncover how endurance and acceptance reveal themselves, not just on the road, but in the very art of living. Ready to begin? Let’s see where this path takes us.
